skill.name: convex-suggest
skill.description: Suggest the matching Convex component when the user hand-rolls a pattern it already solves (crons, sharded-counter, rate-limiter, storage, search, presence, workflow, RAG, prosemirror-sync). Passive — suggest after the task, never interrupt. Never install without consent.
skill.summary: Identifies hand-built Convex patterns and suggests one relevant component after the current task.
skill.author: get-convex

content.value_statement: Developers may rebuild infrastructure that existing Convex components already provide. This skill identifies matching patterns and suggests one focused alternative after completing the current task.
actual_capabilities: Observes Convex code and requests for patterns already handled by supported components.
Matches scheduling, counters, storage, search, presence, workflows, rate limits, and collaborative editing patterns.
Suggests one highest-priority component after the current task is complete.
Explains each recommendation using evidence from the user's code or request.
Provides an installation hint and waits for explicit consent before installation.
Avoids repeating declined suggestions or recommending components already installed.
limitations: The skill recognizes only the patterns and components listed in its detector rules.
It does not install components without explicit user consent.
It does not provide suggestions for generic coding tasks unrelated to Convex.
Recommendations still require developer review for project compatibility and migration effort.

use_cases.title: Reduce custom infrastructure
use_cases.description: Identify an existing Convex component when application code recreates scheduling, storage, search, or workflow features.

use_cases.title: Review scaling patterns
use_cases.description: Spot shared counters, collection scans, and rate-limit logic that may need purpose-built components.

use_cases.title: Guide component adoption
use_cases.description: Give teams one evidence-based recommendation and a clear installation hint without disrupting active work.

prompt_templates.title: Check one code sample
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Convex code and suggest one existing component that replaces a hand-built pattern. Explain the match and wait before installing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a focused recommendation for one snippet.

prompt_templates.title: Review after completing a task
prompt_templates.prompt: After completing my task, inspect these snippets for duplicate infrastructure patterns. Recommend only the highest-priority Convex component and provide its install hint.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants passive guidance during implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare architecture patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my concurrency, scheduling, storage, search, and presence patterns against supported Convex components. Cite the triggering code and avoid already installed components.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead reviews several backend patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit component opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Convex architecture for component opportunities. Rank matches internally, present one recommendation, explain scaling benefits, and install only after explicit consent.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team evaluates component adoption across a system.

output_examples.input: A mutation increments one shared likes value for every request.
output_examples.output: Consider the Convex sharded counter component. The shared increment can create contention at scale. I can provide the installation step after your approval.

output_examples.input: A scheduled action uses a recurring timer for cleanup work.
output_examples.output: Consider the Convex crons component. The recurring timer duplicates managed scheduling behavior. I will not install it unless you approve.

output_examples.input: An application stores uploaded files through a custom external storage path.
output_examples.output: Consider Convex Storage. The upload path matches built-in storage capabilities and may reduce custom integration work. Review migration requirements before adopting it.

best_practices: Provide relevant Convex code and describe the behavior you need.
Evaluate the recommendation against current dependencies, scale, and migration costs.
Approve installation only after confirming the component fits the project.
anti_patterns: Do not request several unrelated component suggestions in one pass.
Do not install a recommendation without reviewing its package and migration requirements.
Do not use this skill for generic code questions unrelated to Convex.

faq.question: Does this skill install Convex components automatically?
faq.answer: No. It waits for explicit consent before running an installation command.

faq.question: When does the skill present a suggestion?
faq.answer: It presents one suggestion after completing the current task, so it does not interrupt active work.

faq.question: Can it recommend several components at once?
faq.answer: It normally recommends only the highest-priority match. It can discuss more components when the user asks.

faq.question: Which patterns can it recognize?
faq.answer: It covers listed patterns for messaging, scheduling, counters, aggregation, workflows, storage, search, presence, RAG, and collaborative editing.

faq.question: Will it suggest components already installed?
faq.answer: No. Its rules require checking for existing installation before making a recommendation.

faq.question: Does it replace architectural review?
faq.answer: No. Developers should verify compatibility, operational needs, and migration effort before adopting a recommendation.
